The *Campakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 348) is a canonical verse biography located in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Like many biographical poems in this collection, it recounts the past meritorious deeds—specifically the pious offering of flowers (*campaka* blossoms)—that led to the elder's eventual spiritual attainment. Five modern translations across five languages are indexed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
No independent parallels are curated by SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language parallels meeting the significance threshold [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, however, DharmaNexus detects widespread textual reuse, recording 66 matching passages across 22 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most extensive reuse occurs in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), where segments §1.2–4.4 correspond to commentary passages (§938–945) [DharmaNexus]. The poem also shares standard devotional formulas with numerous other Apadāna texts centered on flower offerings, including *Kesarapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 366, §2.3–7.1), *Kuṭajapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 519, §0.2–2.1), an earlier homonymous poem *Campakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 138, §5.1–7.1), and *Sattalipupphapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 250) [DharmaNexus].
